faq.a: Selim is associated with the Arabic form سَلِيم, whose core sense is selim; sound, free from defect (turkish form).

faq.q: What is the origin of Selim?
faq.a: Selim is associated with Arabic. Selim is the Turkish form of Arabic سَلِيم (Salīm), meaning 'sound, free from defect'.
Yes — the underlying form سَلِيم is Arabic.
Selim can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Selim should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root س ل م is Quranic, but Salīm is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Selim mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Selim is rendered سلیم and carries the sense سلیم، صحیح سالم.

faq.q: What does Selim mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Selim is rendered سلیم and carries the sense سلیم، تندرست.
A romanized syllable approximation is se-lim. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Selim?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Selim, selim. Script forms are سليم, سلیم, سَلِيم, सेलिम.

faq.q: Is Selim a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
